faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a commercial roof replacement in West Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Yes. New Jersey's 25% rule in N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 treats repairs to up to 25% of the roof area in any 12-month period as ordinary maintenance on a commercial, multi-family, or attached building, so a full replacement needs a construction permit. The NJ Rehabilitation Subcode also requires complete removal of a water-soaked covering or a roof already carrying 2 or more layers, per N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace your West Orange commercial roof?

runs.v: Replace a commercial roof when membrane damage exceeds 25 to 30% of the roof area, when leaks recur at the same location, or when core samples show saturated insulation across a majority of the roof; repair it when damage stays localized. The 25 to 30% threshold traces to Modernize and HomeGuide flat-roof guidance, and a recurring same-spot leak signals systemic failure regardless of damaged area, per HomeAdvisor.

faqs.q: What is the typical lifespan of a new commercial roof?

runs.v: Most commercial membranes need replacement every 15 to 30 years, TPO sometimes sooner, per the InterNACHI chart and Single Ply Roofing Industry guidance. Exposure matters too, since a roof on higher, windier ground can age faster than the same membrane in a sheltered spot.
